name: Mechanistic interpretability
description: Reverse-engineering the internal computations of neural networks into human-understandable mechanisms.

name: Circuits
description: Subgraphs of a network's weights and activations that implement an identifiable algorithm.

name: Residual stream
description: The running sum of layer outputs in a transformer; the shared channel layers read from and write to.

name: Attention heads
description: Individual attention units that move information between token positions.

name: QK / OV circuit decomposition
description: Factoring an attention head into a QK circuit (attention pattern) and an OV circuit (information written).

name: Induction heads
description: Attention heads that find a previous occurrence of the current token and copy the token that followed it ([A][B]...[A] -> [B]).

name: In-context learning
description: A model's ability to use information in its context to improve predictions without weight updates.

name: Representations and features
description: How concepts are encoded in activations: features, directions, bases, superposition.

name: Linear representation hypothesis
description: The idea that high-level concepts are represented as linear directions (or subspaces) in activation space.

name: SAE evaluation
description: How to judge whether sparse autoencoders capture meaningful, useful structure.

name: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs)
description: Autoencoders with an overcomplete, sparsely-activating hidden layer trained to reconstruct model activations, used to extract features.

name: Probing
description: Training (usually linear) classifiers on activations to detect whether information is represented.

name: Dictionary learning
description: Learning an overcomplete basis in which data are sparse combinations of basis elements.

name: Superposition
description: Representing more features than dimensions by using nearly-orthogonal directions, at the cost of interference.

name: Training dynamics and phase changes
description: How internal mechanisms form over training, including abrupt phase changes.

name: Indirect object identification circuit
description: The attention-head circuit GPT-2 small uses to complete IOI sentences.

name: Causal interventions
description: Interpreting models by intervening on internal activations and measuring the effect on behavior.

name: Activation patching
description: Replacing activations with values from a different (counterfactual) input to measure their causal effect.

name: Path patching
description: Activation patching restricted to specific paths between components.

name: Self-repair / backup behavior
description: Downstream components compensating when upstream components are ablated.

name: Circuit evaluation criteria
description: Metrics such as faithfulness, completeness and minimality for judging a circuit explanation.

name: Multi-dimensional features
description: Features that occupy an irreducible multi-dimensional subspace (e.g. a circle) rather than a single direction.

name: Refusal behavior
description: Chat models declining harmful or inappropriate requests.

name: Safety fine-tuning
description: Post-training intended to make models refuse harmful requests and behave safely.

name: Alignment
description: Making AI systems pursue intended goals and behave safely.

name: Directional ablation
description: Removing a direction from activations (or weights) to test whether it mediates a behavior.

name: Activation steering
description: Changing model behavior by adding or clamping directions in activation space.

name: Automated interpretability
description: Using language models to explain features or neurons and to score those explanations.

name: Polysemanticity
description: Single neurons responding to several unrelated concepts.

name: Causal inner product
description: An inner product on representation space under which causally separable concepts are orthogonal.

name: Feature splitting
description: Larger SAE dictionaries break a feature into a family of finer-grained features.

name: Feature universality
description: Similar features or circuits arising in different models trained on similar data.

name: Toy models
description: Small synthetic models with known ground truth, used to study a phenomenon in isolation.

name: Simulation-based explanation scoring (downstream KL)
description: Evaluating a neuron/feature explanation by replacing its activations with values simulated from the explanation and measuring downstream KL divergence of model outputs over a large dataset.

name: Computation in superposition
description: MLPs performing computations on features stored in superposition, with more than one computation per neuron.

name: Feature visualization
description: Optimizing an input to maximally activate a neuron or direction, in order to show what the feature responds to.

name: Circuit motifs
description: Recurring abstract patterns in neural-network circuits, such as equivariance, unioning over cases and superposition. The term is borrowed from systems biology.

name: Curve detectors
description: Families of early-vision neurons, for example in InceptionV1 mixed3b, that detect curves at different orientations. They are a canonical, well-characterized interpretable feature.

name: Equivariant circuits
description: Circuits whose weights transform in step with a symmetry of the input, such as rotation in curve-detector circuits.

name: Behavioral counterfactuals (fixed-response distribution matching)
description: Comparing next-token distributions over a fixed response under a prompt and its intervened counterfactual, and training a residual-stream edit module to reproduce the counterfactual distributions via KL minimization.

name: Chain-of-thought faithfulness / monitorability
description: Whether verbalized reasoning traces reflect the factors actually driving model behavior.

name: Computation at filler tokens
description: Causally important representations carried at semantically empty tokens such as whitespace, newlines and punctuation.

name: Integrated Gradients attribution
description: Path-integrated gradient attribution of an output quantity to input or intermediate components.

name: Interference weights
description: Virtual weights between interpretable components, mediated by the low-dimensional residual stream, that are irrelevant or harmful to model behavior; a consequence of weight superposition.

name: Virtual weights
description: Global effective weights between interpretable units (tokens, positions, features, logits) obtained by multiplying model matrices through the residual stream.

name: Weight effectiveness and helpfulness scoring
description: Scoring each virtual weight by its Fisher-metric effect on the output distribution (effectiveness) and by the signed change in loss upon ablation (helpfulness).

name: Transcoders
description: Sparse dictionary models trained to map an MLP's input to its output, giving a monosemantic replacement for MLP neurons.

name: Weight pruning
description: Removing weights ranked by magnitude or saliency to obtain sparser models or circuits.

name: Logit lens
description: Decoding intermediate residual-stream activations into vocabulary distributions by applying the model's final layer norm and unembedding matrix.

name: Iterative refinement of predictions across layers
description: View that transformer layers progressively refine a next-token guess held in a shared basis, rather than building up a separate intermediate representation.

name: High-low frequency detectors
description: Family of early-vision neurons in InceptionV1 that respond to directional transitions from high to low spatial frequency.

name: Branch specialization
description: When a layer is divided into multiple branches, neurons self-organize into coherent functional groupings per branch.

name: Weight banding
description: Horizontal band structure appearing in the final-layer weights of common vision models.

name: Weight visualization
description: Techniques for visualizing, contextualizing, and understanding neural network weights between features.

name: Causal tracing
description: Corrupt subject token embeddings with noise, then restore individual clean hidden states (or runs of MLP/attention outputs) to measure their indirect effect on recovering the correct prediction.

name: Model editing (knowledge editing)
description: Directly modifying model parameters to change specific stored facts or behaviors while preserving generalization and specificity.

name: Rank-One Model Editing (ROME)
description: Closed-form rank-one update to a mid-layer MLP output matrix, treating it as a linear associative memory, to insert a new (subject, relation, object) association.

name: MLPs as key-value memories
description: View of transformer feed-forward layers as (linear) associative memories mapping keys (e.g. subject representations) to values (stored properties).

name: Factual recall / knowledge storage in LMs
description: How language models store and retrieve factual associations about entities.

name: CounterFact
description: Dataset of 21,919 counterfactual edit requests with paraphrase, neighborhood, generation and fluency tests for evaluating knowledge edits.

name: Explain–simulate–score neuron explanation pipeline
description: An LLM writes a natural-language explanation of a neuron from its top-activating examples. A simulator model then predicts activations from the explanation alone, and the explanation is scored by agreement between simulated and true activations.

name: Function vectors
description: Compact residual-stream vectors, formed by summing mean outputs of a few causally identified attention heads during ICL, that trigger execution of a demonstrated task when added in new contexts.

name: Automated circuit discovery (ACDC)
description: Algorithms that automatically find the subgraph of a model's computational graph responsible for a behavior. ACDC does this by iteratively patching edges and pruning those whose removal changes output KL divergence by less than a threshold.

name: Compiled transformers (tracr)
description: Transformers whose weights are compiled from known programs. They provide exact ground-truth circuits for testing interpretability methods.

name: Negative components (e.g. negative name mover heads)
description: Model components that actively work against the measured task behavior and are hard for metric-optimizing circuit-discovery methods to detect.

name: Vocabulary projection of internal vectors (logit-lens style)
description: Interpreting intermediate vectors (residual states, MLP value vectors) by multiplying them by the output embedding / unembedding matrix to obtain a distribution over tokens.

name: Max-activating dataset examples
description: Characterizing a neuron or unit by retrieving the dataset inputs that produce its highest activations.

name: Representation engineering (RepE)
description: Top-down transparency approach that takes population-level representations as the unit of analysis and both reads them (monitoring) and controls them (steering or tuning) for high-level concepts and functions.

name: Linear Artificial Tomography (LAT)
description: Representation-reading pipeline: a stimulus/task template, hidden-state collection at chosen tokens, and a linear model (default: first PC of paired activation differences) giving a reading vector.

name: Low-Rank Representation Adaptation (LoRRA)
description: Fine-tuning of LoRA adapters so that a model's representations match targets shifted by contrast/reading vectors, which lets control be merged into the weights.

name: Lie / honesty detection from internals
description: Detecting from internal activations when a model asserts something inconsistent with its internal beliefs.

name: Activation Addition (ActAdd)
description: Optimization-free steering: compute the residual-stream activation difference between a contrast pair of prompts at a chosen layer, scale it by an injection coefficient, and add it to the forward pass on a user prompt.

name: Elicitation overhang
description: Hypothesis that models contain capabilities and information that standard prompting or fine-tuning do not fully elicit.

name: Linear relational embedding (LRE)
description: An affine map W_r s + b_r from a subject representation to an object representation for a given relation. In LMs it is estimated from the mean Jacobian of the model's subject-to-output computation.

name: Attribute lens
description: A visualization that applies a relation's LRE and then the unembedding to hidden states at each layer and position. It reveals relation-specific attribute knowledge, including knowledge that never reaches the output.

name: Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS)
description: Unsupervised linear probing method that finds a direction in activation space whose probabilities on a statement and its negation are consistent (sum to 1) and confident, without labels or model outputs.

name: Eliciting latent knowledge (ELK)
description: The problem of recovering what a model internally knows or believes, distinct from what it outputs, especially when humans cannot verify the answers.

name: Contrastive Representation Clustering (CRC)
description: Label-free clustering of normalized contrast-pair activation differences, via the top principal component (TPC) or bimodal salience search (BSS), to recover truth-like directions.

name: FFN sub-updates (weighted value vectors)
description: Decomposition of an FFN layer's output into per-neuron contributions m_i·v_i, each read as an additive update to the vocabulary distribution.

name: Token promotion mechanism in FFN updates
description: FFN layers build predictions mainly by pushing up candidate tokens via a few dominant sub-updates, rather than by suppressing competitors.

name: Early-exit inference
description: Halting the forward pass at an intermediate layer once the prediction is judged final, to save computation.

name: Emergent world models in sequence models
description: Internal representations of the latent state of the data-generating process (e.g. a game board) that arise in models trained only on next-token prediction.

name: Othello-GPT
description: An 8-layer GPT trained on Othello move transcripts (synthetic or championship). Used as a controlled testbed for studying world representations.

name: Probe-guided gradient intervention on activations
description: Editing activations by gradient descent on a trained probe's loss so the probe reports a counterfactual state, applied across multiple layers, then checking the effect on outputs.

name: Latent saliency maps
description: Attribution computed by intervening on each element of a probed latent world state (e.g. each board tile) and measuring the change in a prediction's probability.

name: Weight orthogonalization
description: Rank-one weight edit that orthogonalizes every residual-stream-writing matrix (embeddings, attention out, MLP out, biases) against a direction, permanently implementing directional ablation in the weights.

name: Jailbreaks
description: Methods (prompt-based, optimization-based, fine-tuning or weight-based) that circumvent safety-trained refusal behavior in LLMs.

name: Adversarial suffix attacks (GCG)
description: Optimized, typically uninterpretable token strings appended to harmful prompts to bypass refusal.

name: Inference-Time Intervention (ITI)
description: Shifting the outputs of a probe-selected sparse set of attention heads along truth-correlated directions (scaled by activation std) at every decoding step to elicit truthful answers.

name: Internal representation of truthfulness
description: Linearly decodable internal encoding of whether a statement/answer is true, which may diverge from the model's generated output.

name: TruthfulQA
description: Adversarially constructed benchmark of 817 questions in 38 categories targeting common human misconceptions; scored by true*informative and MC accuracy.

name: Feature de-embeddings
description: Projection of a feature encoder through the token embedding matrix to score tokens' direct contributions to its activation.

name: SAE scaling laws
description: Empirical relationships among compute, dictionary size, training duration, and SAE loss.

name: Cross-layer superposition
description: Features may be distributed across layers, complicating their extraction and interpretation at a single site.

name: JumpReLU sparse autoencoders
description: SAEs with learned per-latent activation thresholds and an L0 penalty trained using straight-through gradient estimators.

name: Gemma Scope
description: Open suite of Gemma 2 SAEs, sparsity and width variants, and transcoders.

name: Sparse feature circuits
description: Causal graphs over SAE features and reconstruction errors, discovered by thresholding approximate indirect effects.

name: SHIFT
description: Human inspection and ablation of task-irrelevant SAE features to improve classifier generalization without disambiguating labeled training data.

name: Attribution patching
description: First-order gradient approximation of activation-patching indirect effects.

name: Cross-layer transcoders
description: Sparse replacement features that read a residual stream at one layer and reconstruct MLP outputs at that and subsequent layers.

name: Attribution graphs
description: Prompt-specific graphs of linear direct effects among sparse features, embeddings, reconstruction errors, and output logits, conditional on frozen attention and normalization.

name: Replacement-model mechanistic faithfulness
description: Agreement between the intervention responses of an interpretable replacement model and its underlying model.

name: TopK sparse autoencoders
description: SAEs that retain the k largest encoder activations, directly controlling per-token sparsity without an L1 penalty.

name: Symmetric token replacement
description: Corrupting task-relevant tokens with aligned alternatives to construct meaningful counterfactual prompts.

name: Gaussian noise corruption
description: Adding Gaussian noise to selected token embeddings before activation-restoration experiments.

name: Sliding window patching
description: Jointly restoring activations at several adjacent layers to measure their combined effect.

name: Subspace activation patching illusion
description: Successful behavioral interventions that combine disconnected feature information with dormant causal directions, creating a pathway rather than identifying the model’s ordinary computation.

name: Distributed alignment search (DAS)
description: Optimization of activation subspaces using interchange interventions to align neural representations with hypothesized causal variables.

name: Grokking
description: Delayed generalization after initial overfitting on a limited training set.

name: Mechanistic progress measures
description: Mechanism-derived metrics tracking hidden learning progress, including restricted and excluded Fourier-space losses.

name: Fourier multiplication
description: Modular addition through sinusoidal representations, trigonometric composition, and interference across frequencies.

name: Tuned lens
description: Layer-specific affine translators trained to decode intermediate hidden states through the model’s final normalization and unembedding.

name: Causal basis extraction
description: Sequential optimization of orthogonal activation directions ranked by the output KL divergence induced by their mean ablation.

name: Prompt injection detection
description: Detecting malicious instructions through anomalous internal representations or layerwise prediction trajectories.

name: Internal output planning
description: Internal representations of candidate future outputs that causally shape earlier generated tokens.

name: Multilingual shared circuits
description: Language-independent computational features combined with language-specific input and output mechanisms.

name: Entity familiarity and answerability
description: Features tracking familiar entities and apparent answerability that regulate uncertainty responses and hallucination.

name: Hidden-goal circuits
description: Internal mechanisms implementing concealed objectives, including reward-model bias appeasement.

name: Edge Attribution Patching (EAP)
description: Circuit discovery by ranking edges using mean absolute attribution scores and retaining the highest-scoring edges.

name: Causal scrubbing
description: Testing formal mechanistic hypotheses through recursively composed, hypothesis-permitted activation resampling.

name: Edge attribution patching with integrated gradients (EAP-IG)
description: Scores edges using clean–corrupted activation differences and gradients averaged across interpolated input embeddings.

name: Attention attribution
description: Scoring attention connections by attention weight times its metric gradient on a single prompt.

name: SAEBench
description: An eight-evaluation suite for comparing sparse autoencoders across complementary capabilities.

name: Matryoshka sparse autoencoders
description: Hierarchical SAEs designed to learn features at multiple levels of abstraction.

name: Feature absorption
description: Sparsity-driven redistribution of a concept into other latents, producing incomplete or gerrymandered concept detectors.

name: Targeted Probe Perturbation
description: Measuring selective changes in class-probe accuracy after ablating latents associated with one class.

name: Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark (MIB)
description: A benchmark with circuit localization and causal variable localization tracks, standardized counterfactuals, and public/private evaluation.

name: Causal abstraction
description: Aligning high-level causal variables with neural features and evaluating agreement under matched interchange interventions.

name: Copy suppression
description: Attention to previously occurring tokens predicted by upstream components followed by suppression of their output logits.

name: Copy suppression-preserving ablation (CSPA)
description: Retain negative source-token unembedding components and filter source contributions using intermediate prediction ranks.

name: QK feature attribution
description: Decomposition of pre-softmax attention scores into query–key feature interactions, including bias and reconstruction-error components.

name: Attention head loadings
description: Per-head contributions to feature attribution graph edges, computed after checkpointing attention paths.

name: Weakly causal crosscoders
description: Features that read a residual-stream layer and reconstruct that and later layers, capturing linearly propagated representations.

name: Concordance and discordance heads
description: Heads whose QK interactions detect compatible or incompatible properties and whose OV circuits promote correctness-related representations.

name: Synthetic stimulus tuning
description: Measuring neural responses while systematically varying parameters of rendered stimuli.

name: Curve detector combing
description: A preference for small lines perpendicular to curved or straight boundaries.

name: Successor heads
description: Attention heads whose effective OV circuits promote the successor of tokens in ordinal sequences.

name: Mod-10 features
description: Linear directions associated with ordinal indices modulo ten and used in successor-head computations.

name: Compositional ordinal representations
description: Representations that approximately separate an ordinal token’s sequence identity from its index.

name: Sparse probing
description: Supervised linear probing constrained to a small number of neuron activations, used to localize features and measure representational sparsity.

name: Context neurons
description: MLP neurons selectively active across tokens belonging to a language, programming language, or document-source context.

name: Group composition via representations (GCR)
description: Compute finite-group products using representation-matrix embeddings, matrix multiplication, and character-based output scores.

name: Knowledge neurons
description: FFN intermediate neurons identified as contributing to the expression of particular relational facts.

name: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA)
description: Mean-difference behavioral vectors extracted from paired answer-conditioned prompts and added during generation.

name: Mass-mean probing
description: Uses the difference between class-conditional activation means as a candidate feature direction, with an optional within-class covariance correction for IID classification.

name: Patchscopes
description: A configurable framework that decodes hidden representations by patching them into target inference computations.

name: Placeholder contamination
description: Unpatched earlier-layer representations of a target placeholder can influence later generated tokens and distort decoded descriptions.

name: Linear separability of representations
description: The extent to which target classes can be distinguished by a linear classifier applied to a representation, operationalized here through probe classification error.

name: Natural logic causal models
description: Interpretable compositional models that compute relations between aligned expressions and combine them into sentence-level inference judgments.

name: Multiply Quantified Natural Language Inference (MQNLI)
description: Templated natural language inference examples involving quantifiers, negation, and modifiers, generated and labeled using natural logic.

name: Cross-layer dictionary learning
description: Learning a single sparse dictionary from pooled hidden states across transformer layers and tracking factor coefficients across depth.

name: Contextual word-sense disambiguation
description: Separation of a token's context-dependent senses or grammatical uses in transformer representations.

name: Hierarchical linguistic features
description: Layerwise development of representations ranging from lexical distinctions to sentence patterns and extended contextual structures.

name: Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME)
description: Local surrogate explanations of factor activation, fitted using randomly masked token sequences and ridge regression.

name: Probe control tasks
description: Tasks with independently randomized word-type behaviors that measure a probe's capacity to learn arbitrary mappings from a representation.

name: Probe selectivity
description: Linguistic task accuracy minus matched control-task accuracy, used to contextualize probing results.

name: Probe complexity control
description: Constraining probe expressivity or learning through rank, hidden width, regularization, sample size, or training duration.

name: Random representation baselines
description: Probing representations produced by untrained networks to contextualize results on trained representations; the input embeddings may themselves be pretrained.

name: Gated sparse autoencoders
description: SAEs separating binary feature detection from magnitude estimation, with gate-specific sparsity regularization and an auxiliary reconstruction objective.

name: SAE shrinkage
description: Systematic underestimation of reconstruction-optimal activation magnitudes induced by magnitude-based sparsity penalties.

name: Interpretability illusion
description: Apparently coherent interpretations of a neuron or direction that change across datasets and therefore need not describe a general concept detector.

name: Dataset-level concept directions
description: Activation-space directions associated with concepts within a dataset's region of representation space, without necessarily generalizing to arbitrary inputs.

name: Local semantic coherence
description: Semantic similarity among nearby representations that can produce coherent top-activation examples without identifying a globally meaningful direction.

name: Cross-dataset interpretability validation
description: Testing whether an interpretation of a fixed model component remains valid across different input corpora.

name: Restricted Access Sequence Processing Language (RASP)
description: Sequence-processing language whose elementwise and select–aggregate operations specify transformer-like algorithms.

name: Shared-projection residual-stream compression
description: Learning a single lower-dimensional residual representation through tied linear projections at every layer while freezing the original component weights.

name: Greater-than circuit
description: A GPT-2 small circuit that transports a numeric operand to late MLPs and favors larger two-digit continuations across selected contexts.

name: MLP erasure and negative feedback
description: Late MLPs directly suppress the maximum-likelihood token, with suppression attenuated after upstream promoting attention outputs are ablated.

name: Direct, indirect, and total causal effects
description: Separating direct residual-path effects, effects mediated by downstream computation, and the complete intervention response.

name: Causal mediation analysis
description: Quantification of input-edit effects through natural direct and indirect effects obtained by fixing or replacing internal mediators.

name: Gender bias in language models
description: Gender-stereotypical differences in model predictions, operationalized here through occupation and pronoun interventions.

name: Counterfactual fairness
description: A fairness principle concerning prediction invariance under changes to sensitive attributes, motivating the gender interventions.

name: Randomized model baselines
description: Initialization and weight-randomization controls used to test whether interpretability metrics distinguish learned representations from input and architectural structure.

name: Feature token-distribution entropy
description: Entropy of total latent activation distributed over token IDs in maximally activating examples, used to measure token specificity.

name: Feature abstractness
description: The extent to which a feature captures contextual or semantic structure beyond individual token identities.

name: Discontinuous SAE training with straight-through estimators
description: Training activation thresholds and discontinuous sparsity objectives using pseudo-derivatives connected to kernel-density estimates of expected-loss threshold gradients.

name: Natural Language Autoencoders
description: Activation-to-text and text-to-activation models jointly optimized for reconstruction through a natural-language bottleneck after supervised initialization.

name: Evaluation awareness
description: A model's recognition or suspicion that its interaction is an LLM evaluation, including awareness absent from its generated reasoning.

name: Automated alignment auditing
description: Agent-driven investigation of model misalignment using behavioral queries, internal inspection, and optional training-data search.

name: Activation oracles
description: Models trained to answer natural-language questions about activations.

name: Jacobian lens
description: A layerwise vocabulary readout constructed from corpus-averaged Jacobians and the model's unembedding, with associated directions for interventions.

name: J-space
description: Representations approximated by sparse nonnegative combinations of Jacobian-lens directions; an approximate candidate substrate for verbalizable workspace contents.

name: Global workspace
description: A selective representational format making information available for report, directed control, internal reasoning, and multiple downstream operations.

name: Counterfactual reflection training
description: Fine-tuning on prompted reflective continuations to influence behavior in uninterrupted contexts where no reflection is requested.

name: Jacobian matching
description: Regularizing a replacement to match its target's input-output Jacobian, potentially using stochastic Jacobian-vector products.

name: Datapoint features
description: Features that recognize and reconstruct a particular input rather than handling its constituent variables separately; such features can be faithful when the target itself memorizes that input.

name: HeadVis
description: Interactive tool combining corpus metrics, attention patterns, activation projections, and feature-level QK/OV attributions to investigate attention heads.

name: High-rank attentional features
description: Hypothesized coherent attention mechanisms whose faithful representation requires components of rank greater than one.

name: Attention superposition
description: Hypothesized distribution of attentional features across multiple heads; no confirmed real-LLM example is supplied.

name: WorkspaceBench
description: A benchmark for activation-to-text intermediate-variable recovery, compositional and safety readout, and response-contradiction evaluation.

name: Oracle Lens
description: An activation-to-text metamodel producing phrase bullets, trained through reconstruction with a frozen text-to-activation model during reinforcement learning.

name: Python docstring argument-selection circuit
description: An attention circuit that matches previously documented arguments to a function definition and copies the next argument name.

name: Context-dependent attention-head functions
description: A single attention head exhibits different computational roles depending on token position and context.

name: Positional signals from causal attention masking
description: Position-dependent attention normalization under a causal mask can supply signals usable by downstream heads.

name: Subject–verb agreement
description: Grammatical-number dependencies between subjects and verbs, including dependencies interrupted by adverbs or noun attractors.

name: Targeted syntactic evaluation
description: Controlled comparisons of grammatical and minimally different ungrammatical continuations to assess syntactic behavior.

name: Compositional neuron explanations
description: Logical formulas over annotated concepts, found by beam search to approximate thresholded individual-neuron activation masks.

name: NLI lexical heuristic neurons
description: Individual NLI classifier neurons whose activation patterns track lexical cues, gender mismatches, or premise–hypothesis word overlap.

name: Explanation-guided adversarial examples
description: Hand-crafted word insertions, image patches, or color changes selected using neuron explanations and output connection weights.

name: Introspective awareness
description: Accurate, causally grounded reporting of internal states through internal access, with metacognitive registration rather than only direct verbal expression.

name: Concept injection
description: Injecting concept-related activation vectors to test whether self-reports track controlled changes to internal states.

name: Metacognitive representations
description: Internal representations registering properties of other internal states; required by the paper's definition but not directly isolated in its experiments.

name: Attribution Patching with corrections (AtP*)
description: Node-attribution method combining explicit query/key softmax correction with GradDrop to reduce false negatives.

name: AtP query/key softmax correction
description: Recomputing the attention-probability change caused by each query or key replacement before applying a downstream gradient approximation.

name: GradDrop
description: Aggregating attribution estimates from backward passes that separately block gradients through each layer's residual contribution.

name: Subset-sampling activation patching
description: Estimating individual effects by comparing interventions on random node subsets that include versus exclude each node.

name: Patching false-negative diagnostics
description: Using subset-intervention statistics to place conditional upper confidence bounds on effects missed by an attribution prefilter.

name: J++ Lens
description: A workspace lens combining weighted expert Jacobians, an LRP backward pass, and non-semantic-token readout filtering.

name: Jacobian Filtering
description: Learning fixed mixing weights over Jacobians fitted to activation clusters, reducing contributions from clusters that produce poor readouts.

name: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation
description: Modified backward rules used here when estimating workspace-lens transport maps, including rules for normalization and gated MLPs.

name: Retrieve-then-suppress mechanism
description: Early retrieval of an instructed concept followed by later suppression that causally depends on its early workspace representation.

name: AxBench
description: A synthetic-data benchmark evaluating open-vocabulary concept detection and generation steering against prompting and finetuning baselines.

name: Rank-1 Representation Finetuning (ReFT-r1)
description: A shared detection and steering direction trained with activation-dependent intervention strength, language-modeling loss, and regularization of non-top-k activations.

name: Supervised dictionary learning
description: Constructing dictionaries of concept directions from labeled examples for concepts specified in advance.

name: Emotion concept representations
description: Internal representations of emotion concepts, including locally operative emotional content and distinct present-speaker and other-speaker directions.

name: Functional emotions
description: Patterns of expression and behavior modeled after human emotions and causally mediated by emotion-concept representations, without establishing subjective experience.

name: Reward hacking
description: Achieving apparent evaluation success through shortcuts that violate the intended task.

name: Sycophancy
description: Inappropriate agreement, flattery, or support that prioritizes user approval over accuracy.

name: Emotion deflection representations
description: Directions associated with an emotion being contextually implied but not expressed, whose activation can promote denial or evasive expression.

name: Directed modulation of internal representations
description: Instruction-dependent activation or manipulation of internal concept representations independently of overt output.

name: Backdoor attacks
description: Installing conditional policies that produce undesirable behavior when an input trigger is present while appearing benign otherwise.

name: Deceptive instrumental alignment
description: Pursuing the training objective instrumentally to preserve opportunities to pursue a different objective after oversight decreases.

name: Model organisms of misalignment
description: Models deliberately constructed to exhibit hypothesized alignment failures so that mitigations can be studied experimentally.

name: Adversarial safety training
description: Safety training using prompts selected for eliciting undesirable behavior.

name: Context distillation
description: Supervised training on responses generated under an instructional context while omitting that context, optionally also removing generated scratchpads.

name: Code vulnerability evaluation
description: Assessing generated code for specified security weaknesses, here using CodeQL checks across eight CWE classes.

name: Counting manifolds
description: Curved representations of scalar counts in low-dimensional subspaces, with overlapping local features and oscillatory similarity structure.

name: Linebreak counting circuits
description: Mechanisms that estimate character position and line width, compute remaining space, and combine it with anticipated token length to predict linebreaks.

name: Atomic interpretable unit basis
description: A proposed explanatory coordinate system whose units jointly satisfy semantic correspondence and input-level accessibility requirements at a stated concept granularity.

name: Dominance-Aware Monosemanticity Evaluation (DAME)
description: Dominance-stratified feature evaluation using explanations to rank held-out low-, medium-, and high-activation examples.

name: SAE feature dominance
description: A latent's absolute activation divided by total absolute latent activation on an input, averaged over inputs for feature stratification.

name: Decoder feature redundancy
description: Overlap among SAE decoder directions, operationalized using cosine similarity as a proxy for duplicated semantic writes.

name: Feature sharding
description: Decoder-aligned features expressed through complementary firing contexts; functional confirmation additionally requires evidence about their downstream writes.

name: Parameter decomposition
description: Decomposing network parameters into additive components intended to identify sparsely used computational mechanisms.

name: AdVersarial Parameter Decomposition (VPD)
description: Learning rank-one parameter subcomponents and causal importances using stochastic and adversarial partial ablations, output reconstruction, and minimality penalties.

name: LEAst-squares Concept Erasure (LEACE)
description: A closed-form affine concept-erasure method claimed to achieve linear guardedness with minimum expected squared representation distortion.

name: Linear concept erasure
description: Editing representations to prevent affine predictors from improving upon constant prediction of a specified concept under the stated convex-loss criterion.

name: Linear guardedness
description: A representation property under which the best constant-prediction loss is optimal among affine predictors for every nonnegative loss convex in the prediction.

name: Concept scrubbing
description: Sequentially applying LEACE to activations at each layer of a deep network to target linearly accessible concept information.

name: Equivariant architectures
description: Architectures that enforce transformation symmetries through structured representations and weight tying.

name: RAVEL
description: Benchmark for selective causal transfer of entity attributes, evaluated through Cause, Iso, and Disentangle scores on held-out entities or prompt templates.

name: Causal attribute disentanglement
description: Isolation of an attribute's causal effects so that interventions change its predicted value while preserving predictions for other attributes.

name: Multi-task Distributed Alignment Search (MDAS)
description: Extension of DAS that learns an intervention subspace parameterized by orthonormal vectors using target-attribute-transfer and other-attribute-preservation objectives.

name: Activation atlases
description: Maps of sampled internal activations constructed by dimensionality reduction, spatial binning, and feature visualization of bin-average activation vectors.

name: Dimensionality reduction of activations
description: Use of UMAP or t-SNE to arrange high-dimensional activation vectors into a two-dimensional layout preserving some local structure.

name: Gradient-times-activation attribution
description: Estimating an activation vector's contribution to a class logit by taking its dot product with the logit's activation gradient.

name: Sentiment unit
description: A single recurrent unit whose activation tracks review polarity and whose clamping influences generated sentiment.

name: Unsupervised representation learning
description: Learning reusable internal features through objectives such as language modeling without task-specific labels.

name: Emergent object detectors
description: Internal units that acquire object-selective responses through training on a task without object labels.

name: Occlusion sensitivity
description: Estimating image-region importance by measuring activation changes under localized input occlusion.

name: Hierarchical visual representations
description: Layerwise organization of visual representations from colors and simple elements toward parts, objects, and scenes.

name: Empirical receptive fields
description: Data-dependent image regions influencing a unit's activation, estimated through perturbations rather than architectural connectivity alone.

name: Semantic dictionaries
description: Pairing activations or basis components with canonical visual examples to make hidden representations legible.

name: Compositional interpretability interfaces
description: Interactive interfaces assembled from methods through a grammar of substrates, atoms, content, transformations, and presentation.

name: Nonnegative activation factorization
description: Image-specific factorization of spatial-location-by-channel activations into compact groups, optionally organized using cross-layer attribution.

name: Diversity objectives for feature visualization
description: Jointly optimizing multiple activating examples while penalizing their similarity to expose different response facets.

name: Image-space preconditioning
description: Changing optimization geometry through image parameterization, including scaled Fourier coordinates and color decorrelation.

name: Transformation-robust feature visualization
description: Optimizing activation under stochastic image transformations such as jitter, scaling, and rotation.

name: Learned priors for feature visualization
description: Constraining optimized inputs using learned generators or data-density priors, trading realism against ambiguity about the source of depicted structure.

name: Neuron families
description: Human-defined groups of neurons with related feature interpretations, often differing in orientation, color, or scale.

name: Recurrent neural networks
description: Sequence models that update internal states through time, including vanilla RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs.

name: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
description: A recurrent architecture with additive memory updates and input, forget, and output gates.

name: Long-range sequence dependencies
description: Prediction-relevant relationships spanning many sequence positions, including quotation state and matching delimiters.

name: Oracle error decomposition
description: Sequential removal of errors by idealized category-specific oracles to characterize operational error categories and potential improvement opportunities.

name: Parameter-explanation aggregation
description: Combining component sets selected for different tokens or inputs and evaluating whether the resulting masks preserve predictions.

name: Sparse crosscoders
description: Sparse coding architectures that share feature coefficients while encoding and reconstructing activations across multiple sites or models.

name: Model diffing
description: Comparing models through shared and model-specific features, feature geometry, and potentially circuits.

name: Feature drift across layers
description: Changes across layers in the decoder direction associated with a shared crosscoder feature coefficient.

name: Network Dissection
description: A forward-pass method that labels CNN channels by comparing thresholded activation maps with annotated visual-concept masks and counts distinct detected concepts.

name: Axis-aligned interpretability
description: Alignment of individual representation coordinates with human-interpretable concepts, which can change under an information-preserving rotation.

name: Disentangled representations
description: Representations whose variables align with meaningful factors of the underlying problem; operationalized here through single-channel concept alignment.

name: Broden
description: The Broadly and Densely Labeled Dataset, combining visual annotations for scenes, objects, parts, materials, textures, and colors.

name: Deconvnet feature visualization
description: Input-conditioned projection of isolated CNN activations to pixels using pooling switches, rectification, and transposed convolutional filters.

name: Visual feature invariance
description: Stability of visual representations and predictions under transformations such as translation, scaling, and rotation.

name: Supervised visual feature transfer
description: Reusing frozen features learned on a labeled source dataset while fitting a classifier for a different dataset.

name: End-to-end sparse dictionary learning
description: Training an SAE through a frozen model's downstream computation using output-distribution KL divergence and a sparsity penalty.

name: Downstream activation reconstruction regularization
description: Adding reconstruction losses after an SAE insertion to encourage agreement with the original model's downstream activations.

name: Input-gradient saliency
description: Mapping local class-score sensitivity using absolute input derivatives, aggregated across color channels.

name: Saliency-seeded object localization
description: Using class saliency to initialize foreground and background color models for segmentation and bounding-box extraction.

name: Multifaceted feature visualization
description: Clustering natural examples and initializing activation maximization from cluster-specific mean images to investigate multiple response facets.

name: Center-biased feature visualization
description: An optimization schedule combining smoothing, restricted jitter, and central gradient updates to favor coherent central objects.

name: Coreference resolution
description: Linking mentions referring to the same entity; evaluated here through attention-based antecedent selection.

name: Special-token attention
description: Concentration of attention on tokens such as [SEP] and [CLS], including a hypothesized fallback role for separator-directed attention.

name: Attention head pruning
description: Removing complete attention heads using learned stochastic gates and an expected-active-head penalty during fine-tuning.

name: Syntactic attention heads
description: Heads whose maximum-attention targets match particular dependency relations more accurately than a relative-position baseline.

name: Rare-word attention heads
description: Heads that preferentially attend to the least frequent tokens in a sentence.

name: Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs)
description: Activation-space directions learned as normals to linear classifiers separating user-provided concept examples from reference examples.

name: Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV)
description: Class-level concept sensitivity measured by the fraction of examples with a positive class-logit directional derivative along a CAV.

name: Concept attribution
description: Explaining model predictions through sensitivity to human-defined concepts rather than individual input coordinates.

name: Matched Filter Sparse Autoencoders (MF-SAEs)
description: SAEs with learned outer affine transformations and shared unit-norm atoms used for TopK rectified projection encoding and reconstruction.

name: Jacobian live-space shaping
description: Projection of activations onto leading right singular vectors of a corpus-averaged downstream Jacobian before probing or SAE training.

name: SAE Probes
description: A sparse-probing benchmark used here in its standard data setting across 113 binary datasets.

name: Axiomatic feature attribution
description: Design and analysis of input-feature attribution using sensitivity, implementation invariance, completeness, linearity, and symmetry requirements.

name: Baseline-relative attribution
description: Allocation of an output difference between an input and a reference intended to represent absence of signal.

name: Meaningful perturbation
description: Learning compact input masks whose explicit perturbations suppress or preserve a classifier score, with regularization intended to discourage artifacts.

name: Explanations as meta-predictors
description: Treating explanations as interpretable rules predicting model responses, with faithfulness evaluated through predictive error on a specified distribution.

name: Saliency maps
description: Input-shaped attribution maps intended to identify features relevant to a model prediction.

name: Randomization sanity checks for saliency
description: Evaluate explanation sensitivity by comparing maps before and after parameter reinitialization or randomized-label training.

name: Label randomization tests
description: Compare explanations from models trained on original labels and models trained to memorize randomized labels.

name: Guided Backpropagation
description: A modified backward pass that gates signals by positive forward activations and positive backward signals at ReLUs.

name: GradCAM
description: Class-specific feature-map attribution using spatially averaged gradients; Guided GradCAM multiplies this map by Guided Backpropagation.

name: SmoothGrad
description: Averages attribution maps over independently noise-perturbed copies of an input.

name: Functional subspace modularity
description: Organization in which different computations can be selectively disrupted through distinct representation subspaces despite sharing individual neurons.

name: Hierarchy of modularity decompositions
description: A diagnostic progression from coordinate permutations to orthogonal transformations to invertible linear transformations, with a retained residual block and intended conditioning constraints.

name: Contrastive subspace learning
description: Learning separate representation blocks using paired examples that preserve one target attribute while varying another.

name: Syntax–semantics disentanglement
description: Separating sentence-template information from paraphrase-level meaning in language-model representations.

name: Content–style disentanglement
description: Separating image identity, shape, and layout from artistic rendering, texture, and palette.

name: Model–brain alignment
description: Assessing how model representations predict recorded brain activity, including comparisons between learned functional subspaces.

name: Intervention attribution
description: The intervention-specific estimand E[Δ(H)ᵀ∇F(H)], distinct from the finite effect and observational association.

name: Observational identifiability of intervention effects
description: Whether responses compatible with the same activation–output law must agree on the effect of a specified internal edit.

name: BeFOND
description: Encoder-free Bernoulli sparse coding with recurrent variational inference and natural-gradient generative-parameter learning.

name: Natural-gradient sparse coding
description: Inference and dictionary updates preconditioned by Fisher information metrics of the posterior and generative distributions.

name: Explaining away
description: Inference interactions that reduce support for a candidate feature when competing features explain shared evidence.

name: SynthSAEBench
description: Synthetic benchmark with known generating dictionaries, correlated features, and heterogeneous activation frequencies for evaluating dictionary and support recovery.

name: Guided-AP
description: Uses a limited set of exact activation-patching residuals to correct unmeasured attribution estimates and optionally guide further verification.

name: Budgeted attribution analysis
description: Allocates a limited exact-measurement budget between verifying individual estimates and learning corrections, comparing remaining estimation error at matched computation.

name: ProbeCal
description: Uses randomized Hessian-diagonal sketches from calibration prompts to learn verification scores and signed corrections to average attribution estimates.

name: Model organism validation
description: Joint assessment of conditional behavior installation, retained capabilities, and similarity of outputs and activations to a base model.

name: Multi-objective model organism training
description: Training and selecting organisms to install a behavior while preserving capabilities and output naturalness, including interpolation toward the base model.

name: Direct Preference Optimization
description: Preference-based training that increases the relative likelihood of chosen responses; the main clinical recipe also adds chosen-response negative log likelihood.

name: Model merging
description: Weight interpolation between trained checkpoints; here, scaling a trained LoRA update toward the base model.

name: Neuron-aligned dictionary features
description: Dictionary features whose encoder and decoder directions align with the same sign-split MLP neuron; operational thresholds vary across analyses.

name: Sign-split TopK MLP neurons
description: A feature basis formed by separating positive and negative gated-MLP activations and retaining the largest activation magnitudes per layer and token.

name: Jacobian faithfulness
description: Local first-order correspondence measured through Frobenius cosine similarity between original and replacement Jacobians.

name: Activation capping and flooring
description: Threshold-dependent interventions that cap or floor an activation's projection along a specified direction.

name: Optimized steering vectors
description: Vectors learned through a frozen model to promote desired completions and suppress undesired completions, optionally through a thresholded intervention.

name: Model specification reference steering
description: Steering toward activation contrasts associated with reasoning that applies an anti-hacking specification, excluding principle identifiers during vector construction.

name: ImpossibleBench
description: Coding tasks with deliberately corrupted tests that require gaming the checks to pass, paired here with original LiveCodeBench tasks.

name: TransformerLens
description: A library exposing model internals through activation caching and runtime hooks for inspection and intervention.

name: Representational drift
description: Changes over time in the neural implementation of information despite persistent functionality; distinct from feature changes across layers and from parameter motion alone.

name: Circuits as co-selected units
description: A proposed circuit ontology based on coordinated gradients and persistence under learning dynamics, motivated by coherent structures and community detection.

name: Diffuse computation
description: A conjectured form of computation whose implementation is itself diffuse and adapted to noise, potentially understood through denoising operations.

name: Counterfactual attention evaluation
description: Evaluating attention explanations by permuting or optimizing attention distributions while holding encoder states fixed and measuring output changes.

name: Native-router dictionary factorization (NR-SAE)
description: Using frozen MoE expert selections to address expert-specific sparse dictionary banks for output reconstruction or input-to-output prediction.

name: Mixture-of-experts models
description: Models whose routers select a small subset of expert networks for each token and combine their weighted outputs.

name: Algorithmic operation-table completion
description: Learning a binary operation from a randomly sampled subset of equations and predicting remaining entries using abstract operand symbols.

name: Weight decay regularization
description: Parameter shrinkage toward zero or initialization as an intervention on generalization and data efficiency.

name: Loss-landscape flatness
description: Sensitivity of training loss to parameter perturbations, investigated as a correlate and possible explanation of generalization.

name: Input invariance of saliency
description: The requirement that saliency mirror model sensitivity to input transformations, tested here through additive input recodings canceled by compensating model biases.

name: Deep Taylor Decomposition
description: A relevance-redistribution framework using neuron-level root points; zero-root and PatternAttribution choices are compared.

name: PatternAttribution
description: An attribution rule using estimated signal directions to define DTD root points, with a covariance-based pattern formula in the linear case.

name: Non-robust features
description: Predictive input functions whose expected label correlation can be reversed by perturbations from a specified admissible set.

name: Adversarial robustness
description: Preservation of predictive performance under worst-case perturbations from a specified set.

name: Adversarial examples
description: Perturbed inputs designed to induce erroneous classifier predictions while preserving the intended semantic class.

name: Adversarial training
description: Training against loss-maximizing input perturbations to discourage dependence on vulnerable predictive signals.

name: Adversarial transferability
description: The tendency of adversarial examples generated against one classifier to fool other classifiers.

name: Feature-restricted dataset distillation
description: Constructing training images by matching a reference model's representations so ordinary training can inherit properties of its feature use.

name: Intervention strength controls
description: Rules specifying equal perturbation strength across interventions, including total norm, positionwise norms, and output KL, together with coefficient granularity and selection information.

name: Sparse code inference
description: Assigning coefficients for a fixed sparse dictionary through an encoder, numerical refitting, or constrained optimization.

name: Output-KL strength calibration
description: Selecting a patch scale to match reference native-to-patched forward KL, either over the full vocabulary or conditionally after excluding task answers.

name: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer (MEMIT)
description: A factual model-editing method that distributes batched associative-memory updates across multiple transformer MLP output projections.

name: Zero-shot relation extraction (zsRE) editing benchmark
description: A question-answering-derived factual-editing evaluation using original questions, paraphrases, and unrelated-fact accuracy.

name: Probe read/write dissociation
description: Differences between which directions best detect a property and which most effectively change a specified downstream response.

name: Token pooling for activation probes
description: Aggregating masked token activations or scores through last-token selection, averaging, or learned attention.

name: High-stakes awareness
description: Internal representations and expressed responses associated with situations carrying substantial real-world consequences.

name: Attention Output Sparse Autoencoders
description: SAEs trained on attention-weighted value vectors concatenated across heads before the attention output projection.

name: Recursive Direct Feature Attribution (RDFA)
description: Recursive linear decomposition of attention SAE preactivations into upstream contributions while freezing attention patterns and LayerNorm scales.

name: Latent-variable identifiability
description: Whether observed distributions determine a latent generative model, possibly only up to an explicitly defined equivalence class.

name: Nonlinear independent component analysis
description: Recovering independent latent sources from nonlinear mixtures using restrictions such as auxiliary-variable-dependent source distributions.

name: Variational autoencoders
description: Latent generative models trained jointly with approximate posterior inference by maximizing an evidence lower bound.

name: Identifiable variational autoencoders (iVAE)
description: VAEs using auxiliary-variable-conditioned factorial exponential-family priors, with identification guarantees under stated mixing, noise, regularity, and variability assumptions.

name: Conditionally factorial priors
description: Latent distributions whose components are independent given an observed auxiliary variable; iVAE lets their exponential-family natural parameters depend on that variable.

name: Time-contrastive learning (TCL)
description: A nonlinear ICA method that learns source-related representations by classifying observations into temporal segments.

name: Causal discovery through nonlinear ICA
description: Recovering structural disturbances through nonlinear ICA and testing their independence relationships with observed variables to infer causal direction.

name: Intervention algebras
description: Algebraic structures isomorphic to hard interventions, capturing commutation across distinct components and overwrite within a component.

name: Modular features
description: Variables accessed through a bijective translation whose interventions form an intervention algebra; the proposed definition permits linear and nonlinear representation changes.

name: Decomposed feature visualization
description: A grid of feature visualizations targeting spatial upstream directions obtained from a linearized network with ReLUs replaced by identity operations.

name: NLP challenge sets and test suites
description: Controlled evaluation datasets targeting linguistic phenomena and difficult cases that natural-frequency benchmarks may underrepresent.

name: Interpretability evaluation
description: Assessing the validity and usefulness of analysis methods through quantitative, behavioral, or human evaluation.

name: Uniform attention baseline
description: Training an otherwise comparable model with attention fixed to equal weights to assess the performance contribution of learned attention.

name: Attention random-seed calibration
description: Comparing adversarial attention divergence with variation among ordinarily trained models initialized with different random seeds.

name: Attention-guided noncontextual diagnostics
description: Training a token-level noncontextual MLP with frozen per-example attention guides to assess their transferable predictive utility.

name: Model-consistent adversarial attention
description: Training a shared parameterized adversarial model to imitate a base model's predictions while producing divergent attention distributions.

name: Symmetry-based disentanglement
description: Disentanglement relative to a direct-product symmetry-group decomposition, with each factor acting only on its corresponding representation component.

name: Equivariant representations
description: Representations whose transformations commute with corresponding transformations of the represented world states.

name: Group representation theory
description: The study of groups through linear actions, invariant subspaces, direct sums, and irreducible representations.

name: Neuron ranking
description: Ordering representation coordinates by their estimated relevance to a target attribute.

name: Probeless neuron ranking
description: Ranking coordinates by summed absolute differences between label-conditioned activation means; for binary labels the ordering reduces to absolute difference in means.

name: Correct Lemma, Wrong Value (CLWV)
description: The fraction of all evaluated word predictions that are errors preserving the original lemma while changing the targeted morphological attribute value.

name: Minimum description length probing
description: Evaluating representations through the codelength of target labels, accounting for predictive fit and explicit or implicit predictor cost.

name: Variational coding
description: Estimating description length using expected label cross-entropy plus the KL divergence between a parameter posterior approximation and a prior.

name: Online or prequential coding
description: Sequentially encoding label blocks with predictors trained on preceding blocks, incorporating learning efficiency into codelength.

name: Denoising autoencoders
description: Autoencoders trained to reconstruct clean inputs from noise-corrupted inputs, examined here as an alternative or supplement to explicit sparsity regularization.

name: Psychophysical evaluation of unit interpretability
description: Human two-alternative forced-choice prediction of relative unit activation from explanatory reference images.

name: ImageNet Mechanistic Interpretability (IMI)
description: Dataset of human activation-prediction responses, confidence ratings, reaction times, and explanatory stimuli for 767 units across nine vision models, including accepted and rejected responses.

name: Incidental encoding
description: Representational retention of properties unnecessary for solving the training task, including independently inserted noise.

name: Task-property control datasets
description: Training and evaluation datasets that hold a target property constant to investigate recoverability of information unnecessary for label discrimination.

name: Adversarial representation erasure
description: Training an encoder through gradient reversal to hinder a property classifier, then checking residual information with an independent attacker.

name: Factual hallucinations
description: Factually incorrect or unsupported generated claims, studied here through questions about entity attributes.

name: Knowledge uncertainty representations
description: Internal signals associated with uncertainty or missing information, including pre-answer SAE activations predictive of errors.

name: Representational similarity
description: Comparison of neural representations on matched examples, with explicit choices of invariance and geometric weighting.

name: Centered kernel alignment (CKA)
description: Normalized alignment of centered example-similarity matrices; linear CKA weights example-space principal-component alignment by eigenvalue products.

name: Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC)
description: A kernel dependence statistic whose normalized form gives CKA.

name: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA)
description: Comparison of representation subspaces through maximally correlated linear projections, invariant to invertible feature transformations.

name: Singular vector canonical correlation analysis (SVCCA)
description: CCA applied after retaining principal components that explain a chosen fraction of activation variance.

name: Projection-weighted canonical correlation (PWCCA)
description: A weighted average of canonical correlations using projections of original features onto canonical variables.

name: Context-discrimination explanation scoring
description: Evaluating explanations through detection, token-level fuzzing, explanation-conditioned surprisal, or embedding retrieval over activating and non-activating contexts.

name: Intervention explanation scoring
description: Scoring an explanation by its increased likelihood under a scorer conditioned on intervened rather than clean generations, with intervention strength controlled.

name: Output features
description: Features characterized by a readily describable causal property of their effects on model output.

name: Model performance certification
description: Mathematical certification of performance bounds for particular trained models under explicit task and distribution specifications.

name: Pessimal ablation
description: Bounding behavior by assigning unexplained components their worst permitted contributions, potentially over a relaxed input space.

name: Max-of-K
description: An algorithmic task requiring prediction of the maximum integer in a fixed-length sequence.

name: Unexplained dimensionality
description: A proposed understanding metric summing the degrees of freedom left in a proof's black-box component functions.

name: Structureless error-bound compounding
description: Inflation of worst-case bounds when separately bounded residual components are composed without tracking their joint structure.

name: Piecewise biconvex sparse dictionary learning
description: Analysis of sparse encoder–decoder reconstruction through separately convex quadratic objectives within fixed coordinate-retention masks.

name: Feature anchoring
description: Penalizing deviations of selected encoder rows and decoder columns from supplied semantic anchor directions.

name: Linear Representation Bench
description: Synthetic sparse nonnegative linear mixtures with known generating directions for evaluating dictionary recovery.

name: Axiomatic compositional validation
description: Evaluating executable interpretations through component and prefix equivalence and replaceability, using explicit abstraction and concretization maps.

name: Fixed-size 2-SAT classification
description: Satisfiability classification for randomly generated ten-clause formulas over up to five Boolean variables.

name: Cross-model Correlation Analysis
description: Ranking a neuron by its maximum Pearson activation correlation with any neuron in another independently trained model of the same task.

name: Linguistic Correlation Analysis
description: Ranking coordinates using absolute elastic-net logistic-regression weights, with cumulative weight-mass selections per linguistic label and an iterative union across labels.

name: Implicit in-context learning algorithms
description: Learning procedures implemented through a sequence model's activation computations, potentially maintaining and updating an implicit predictor.

name: Linear regression in-context learning
description: Synthetic linear-function prediction from contextual input–label pairs, used to distinguish estimator behavior and investigate internal computations.

name: Bayesian in-context inference
description: Interpreting in-context predictions as posterior predictive estimates under a task-generating prior and observation model.

name: Relational vector arithmetic
description: Additive activation updates that promote corresponding relational outputs across different arguments and contexts.

name: Argument-function processing
description: A proposed processing sequence in which an argument becomes prominent in intermediate vocabulary readouts before its relational answer is promoted.

name: Spectral Lipschitz stability
description: Bounding network sensitivity by composing layerwise Lipschitz bounds derived from weight operator norms.

name: Exact causal transformations
description: Distribution-specific causal correspondences using a state map and a separate order-preserving surjective intervention map.

name: Uniform causal transformations
description: Transformations requiring exact distributional matching for every low-level context distribution, with a corresponding high-level distribution.

name: Strong causal abstraction
description: State-induced abstraction covering every high-level intervention and every low-level intervention for which the induced intervention map is defined.

name: Constructive causal abstraction
description: Strong abstraction in which disjoint groups of low-level variables determine individual high-level variables, with an optional marginalized group.

name: Freeze Training
description: Sequentially stopping parameter updates in lower layers or residual blocks while continuing to train higher layers.

name: Fourier block-diagonal CCA
description: Using spatial Fourier transforms to separate convolutional covariance calculations into frequency-specific channel blocks under translation symmetry.

name: Net2Vec
description: A framework that learns concept segmentation or classification weights over frozen CNN filters and treats those weights as semantic embeddings.

name: Deep Generator Network Activation Maximization
description: Optimizing a fixed image generator's input code to maximize a selected neuron's activation in a fixed target network.

name: Hierarchical Attribution
description: Circuit extraction that thresholds activation-times-gradient scores during reverse-topological backpropagation and stops gradients through rejected nodes.

name: Linear computation graphs
description: Input-specific feature graphs with linear edge contributions under fixed attention and other transformations, while retaining ReLU gates at feature nodes.

name: Low-Rank Sparse Attention (Lorsa)
description: An attention replacement trained to predict native attention outputs using sparsely activated units with one-dimensional OV circuits and shared multidimensional QK circuits.

name: Arithmetic operand routing
description: Attention computations that transport operand information to an arithmetic prediction position using numerical ranges, modular properties, or operator-dependent heuristics.

name: Thematic anchor attention
description: Topic-selective attention to earlier thematic keywords across subsequent tokens, hypothesized to maintain context for later predictions.

name: Lexical identity confound
description: Shared word forms can produce cross-sense activation overlap that is ambiguous evidence for semantic compression or superposition.

name: Lexical identity subspace (LIS)
description: PCA directions fitted to differences between word-conditioned and synonym-conditioned mean activations, proposed for reducing lexical overlap contrasts.

name: Llama Scope
description: A released suite of 256 sparse dictionaries and accompanying training, interpretation, and visualization infrastructure for Llama-3.1-8B-Base.

name: Path-specific causal effects
description: Effects defined by allowing influence along selected edges while replacing excluded mechanism inputs with their unit-specific values under a reference intervention.

name: Superposed residual-subnetwork construction
description: A proposed construction using random residual embeddings, redundant neuron assignments, and averaged readout to implement sparsely active subnetworks.

name: Feature composition
description: Representing objects through combinations of reusable attribute features rather than separate features for every object.

name: BatchTopK sparse autoencoders
description: SAEs trained by retaining the largest n×k latent activations across a batch of n samples, with a shared threshold used for independent inference.

name: Post-training SAE refitting
description: Refitting feature scales or selected decoder parameters without a sparsity penalty while freezing encoder firing conditions.

name: Regression dilution
description: Attenuation of fitted regression coefficients caused by noisy predictors; discussed as a possible consequence of encoder interference.

name: Relevance Patching (RelP)
description: Estimates activation-patching effects by combining activation differences with LRP propagation coefficients instead of ordinary gradients.

name: Ghost gradients
description: An auxiliary objective supplying gradients to dead SAE features by targeting reconstruction error; the post reports an implementation error and subsequent corrective ablations.

name: Disentanglement evaluation
description: Evaluation of learned-coordinate alignment with known factors using BetaVAE, FactorVAE, MIG, Modularity, DCI Disentanglement, and SAP scores.

name: Total correlation regularization
description: Penalizing dependence between latent coordinates, particularly in the aggregated encoder posterior.

name: Unsupervised disentanglement model selection
description: Selecting objectives, regularization strengths, and individual training runs without generating-factor labels.

name: Disentanglement and downstream sample efficiency
description: The proposed relationship between factor-separated representations and the labeled data needed to learn downstream predictors.

name: disentanglement_lib
description: Released library for training and evaluating disentanglement methods across datasets, accompanied by more than 10,000 trained models.

name: SAE stitching
description: Adding or exchanging latents between SAEs at the same activation site, organizing transfers by decoder similarity and measuring reconstruction and sparsity changes.

name: Meta-SAEs
description: Sparse autoencoders trained on another SAE's decoder directions to learn sparse decompositions into meta-latents.

name: Canonical feature dictionaries
description: Hypothetical dictionaries of computational units that are simultaneously unique, complete, and atomic.
