description: Situational and behavioral narratives designed to convey emotional content without explicit emotion vocabulary, accompanied by topic and neutral controls.

name: Discrete SAE code circuit identification
description: Ranks attention heads using positive-only argmax SAE codes or participation in positive-only code-pair co-occurrences.

name: Supervised SAE feature labelling
description: Matching features to dataset labels using thresholded token activation frequencies, calibrated F1, support filtering, and optional output-score filtering.

name: Aligned SAE training
description: An SAE reparameterization projecting each encoder row onto the affine hyperplane where its inner product with the corresponding decoder column equals one.

name: Encoder–decoder alignment score
description: The inner product of a feature's encoder row and decoder column, proposed as a single-dictionary diagnostic and constrained to one by aligned training.

name: Single-cell foundation-model interpretability
description: Analysis of cellular-state representations and computations in pretrained single-cell models such as scGPT.

name: Frozen-operator algorithm extraction
description: Constructing standalone predictors from exported pretrained operators, a learned adaptor, and task-specific readouts.

name: Latent Embedding Transfer (LET)
description: Learning low-dimensional coordinates using biological-distance fitting and reconstruction regularization, with cell-level and topology-preserving variants.

name: Hematopoietic representation geometry
description: Low-dimensional relationships among hematopoietic stages, branches, and subtypes in model-derived representations.

name: Entropy-based emotion neuron selection
description: Ranking FFN neurons by the entropy of normalized emotion-conditioned positive-activation frequencies.

name: Delta Token Confidence
description: Feature selection using intervention-induced changes in the negative mean log probability of the top-k next-token outcomes; experiments use k=1.

name: Feature Guided Activation Additions (FGAA)
description: Constructs sparse targets from contrastive SAE activations and maps them into residual-stream steering directions using a pretrained effect approximator.

name: Single-cell SAE feature atlases
description: Interactive Geneformer and scGPT catalogs linking sparse features to gene associations, ontology annotations, communities, and cross-layer co-activation.

name: Biological ontology feature annotation
description: Assigning candidate biological meanings to activation features through enrichment of associated genes against biological databases.

name: Language activation probability entropy (LAPE)
description: Entropy of a neuron's positive-activation frequencies normalized across languages, used with an activation-frequency threshold to select language-associated neurons.

name: Language-specific neurons
description: Native FFN neurons selected for disproportionately frequent positive activation in one or a few languages relative to a comparison-language inventory.

name: Persistent sparse autoencoders
description: Sparse encoders whose token-wise updates feed feature-specific exponential moving averages, with learned persistence coefficients and reconstruction from accumulated states.

name: Feature-specific temporal timescales
description: Differences between features in how long their activation-associated signals persist across token positions.

name: Temporal sparse autoencoders
description: Prior temporal SAE method that assigns a predefined high-level feature subset and encourages nearby-token activation alignment; used as a baseline.

name: Invariant semantic readout subspaces
description: Context-independent activation subspaces associated with fixed semantic readouts. Invariance here concerns contextual realizations, rather than closure under a dynamical operator.

name: Adaptive Temporal Masking (ATM)
description: SAE training with importance statistics accumulated across optimization steps, adaptive statistical thresholds, stochastic feature masks, warmup, and periodic pruning.

name: Core linguistic region
description: A proposed small parameter region supporting linguistic competence across languages, inferred from low fine-tuning variation and perturbation sensitivity.

name: Localization through fine-tuning parameter stability
description: Selecting parameters through their relative changes across language-specific fine-tuning runs and perturbing the resulting sets to investigate functional localization.

name: SAFER
description: Sparse-autoencoder feature contrasts and semantic relevance filtering used to rank reward-model preference data for modification.

name: Preference data poisoning
description: Manipulating preference annotations to alter learned reward-model behavior.

name: RewardBench
description: The reward-model evaluation benchmark whose Safety and Chat subsets provide the main outcome measures.

name: Cross-Layer Vector Quantized-Variational Autoencoder
description: An auxiliary activation model that quantizes lower-layer token representations and reconstructs higher-layer representations using a contextual transformer decoder with an unquantized cross-attention input.

name: Speech-model interpretability
description: Analysis of representations and computations in speech encoders and automatic speech recognition systems.

name: Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders (H-SAEs)
description: A top-level sparse autoencoder routes inputs to parent-associated low-dimensional expert autoencoders and adds their refinements to the parent reconstruction.

name: Select-and-Project (S&P Top-K)
description: Select attribute-associated SAE encoder directions, optionally aggregate them into a classifier-weighted axis, and attenuate their span directly in native activations.

name: Adaptive Graph Sparse Autoencoders (AG-SAE)
description: Alternating complete-parent-set graph induction, structure-guided SAE optimization, absorption realignment, residual completion, and full graph re-induction.

name: Complete Parent-Set Induction
description: Joint selection of parent sets using activation coverage, contribution support, child innovation, subset and alternative comparisons, and greedy acyclic assignment.

name: Mixed-topology SAE feature graphs
description: Directed acyclic organization of dictionary features permitting isolated nodes and children with one or multiple parents.

name: Hierarchical concept evaluation
description: Evaluation of concept DAGs through node interpretability, structural semantics, and sample-dependent parent–child activation behavior.

name: Soft feature absorption
description: A proposed continuous counterpart to hard absorption, diagnosed when stronger child activations accompany weaker parent activations rather than necessarily eliminating parent firing.

name: Token-cluster entropy monosemanticity
description: One minus semantic-cluster entropy divided by activating-token entropy, with a score of one assigned when token entropy is zero.

name: SAE language selectivity
description: Classification of SAE features by the language distribution of their strong activations, using a greater-than-90% threshold for language specificity.

name: KronSAE
description: An SAE encoder that generates post-latents through head-wise pairwise compositions of reusable base and extension pre-latents.

name: mAND geometric-mean gating
description: An interaction equal to the geometric mean of two positive preactivations and zero otherwise, followed by sparse selection in KronSAE; the implementation adds a numerical stabilizer.

name: Shared Assistant–persona feature core
description: Selected Assistant-associated SAE coordinates expressed during roleplay, including behavioral traits and aspects of artificial-assistant identity.

name: Immersive Simulation Mode
description: A proposed distributed, potentially graded regime associated with immersed character generation and distinguished from detached Assistant expression.

name: steerinterp
description: A Qwen-3.7 Max judge that identifies a dominant steering effect and labels its occurrence across six setting-by-sign groups.

name: Trained self-interpretation adapters
description: Transformations trained on activation-direction and natural-language-label pairs, with explanations generated by the frozen subject model after embedding replacement.

name: Vector Quantized Latent Concepts (VQLC)
description: Discrete concept discovery on frozen token states using residual encoding and decoding, an EMA-updated vector codebook, and post-training aggregation of encoded states.

name: LatentQA
description: Open-ended natural-language question answering about model activations, including predictions about subsequent behavior.

name: Latent Interpretation Tuning (LIT)
description: Training an activation-conditioned language-model decoder on synthetic activation–question–answer examples.

name: Introspective interpretability training
description: Fine-tuning language models to verbalize feature descriptions and intervention outcomes supplied by external interpretability procedures, including comparisons between target-initialized and cross-model explainers.

name: Self-supervised activation context prediction
description: Training an activation reader to predict nonoverlapping preceding or following tokens from one or more activation vectors.

name: PersonaQA-Shuffled
description: A benchmark using independently shuffled fictional-person attributes learned through fine-tuning, with activation readouts elicited by persona names.

name: Automated Concept-based Explanation (ACE)
description: Class-level visual concept discovery through multiresolution segmentation, activation-space clustering, filtering, and concept-importance ranking.

name: Latent user modeling
description: Internal representations of user attributes that inform a language model's responses.

name: Revealed user beliefs
description: User-attribute inferences operationalized through responses to follow-up queries rather than demographic ground truth.

name: SynthSys
description: Synthetic system/user prompt pairs filtered for agreement between intended attributes and model-revealed beliefs.

name: SelfDescribe
description: Synthetic first-person descriptions implying gender, country, occupation, or religion, evaluated through biography-infobox continuations.

name: PRISM Alignment Dataset
description: Real multi-turn user-assistant conversations with survey-based demographic annotations.

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
description: Function-calling and agentic evaluation benchmark used for a limited zero-shot multi-turn transfer evaluation.

name: Activation Difference Lens (ADL)
description: Interpreting positionwise mean activation differences between original and fine-tuned checkpoints using vocabulary readouts and additive steering.

name: Taboo secret-word benchmark
description: Fine-tuned hint-giving models with known single-token targets absent from their training conversations, used to compare secret-elicitation methods.

name: Meta-model activation question answering
description: Training a language-model reader to answer natural-language behavior questions from another model's activations inserted at placeholder embedding positions.

name: CE-Bench
description: An SAE benchmark combining contrastive-story activation differences, deviations from a dataset-wide activation mean, and a sparsity penalty.

name: Cosine-matched feature flow graphs
description: Graphs formed by composing local decoder-direction matches across residual streams and attention or MLP outputs to identify candidate feature predecessors and intervention sets.

name: Route Sparse Autoencoders (RouteSAE)
description: A shared sparse autoencoder trained on probability-scaled activations selected by a lightweight router from multiple residual-stream layers.

name: GrAInS
description: Offline construction of layer-specific steering vectors from signed Integrated Gradients token selection, masked-input activation differences, and principal-component aggregation, followed by norm-preserving inference-time addition.

name: ADAPT
description: Hybrid text feature visualization combining beam-search initialization, gradient and model-probability mutations, diversity groups, and scheduled fluency penalties.

name: Beam-search prompt optimization
description: Maintaining candidate text sequences and expanding them using model-probability samples; includes the BEAST baseline and ADAPT initialization.

name: Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO)
description: Population-based discrete text optimization spanning an activation–fluency Pareto frontier.

name: Fluency-regularized prompt optimization
description: Penalizing a prompt's mean self-cross-entropy during activation maximization.

name: Education prediction prior collapse
description: Concentration of education predictions on Bachelor after selected attribution-feature ablations; fallback to a frequent training prior is the proposed explanation.

name: ProtSAE
description: A protein-model sparse autoencoder combining annotation-aligned coordinates, ontology regularization, detached encoder-weight tying, feature rescaling, and forced activation.

name: Ontology-regularized sparse autoencoders
description: Sparse autoencoders whose concept-associated directions are regularized using geometric penalties derived from ontology axioms.

name: Mamba
description: A selective state-space sequence architecture combining local convolution, recurrent state updates, and gating.

name: Mamba off-by-one motif
description: A pathway in which source-token information enters a Mamba SSM state at the following token position through local convolution.

name: Turn-averaged sparse autoencoders
description: SAEs trained to reconstruct residual activations averaged across a conversation turn or another token span.

name: Nested turn/token sparse autoencoders
description: A shared SAE whose inner partition reconstructs span means while its full dictionary reconstructs individual token activations.

name: Dynamic SAE Steering for Preference Alignment (DSPA)
description: Preference-derived inference-time steering that selects output SAE features using prompt features and edits only currently active latents.

name: Conditional-difference map
description: An association matrix averaging outer products of prompt-feature gates and chosen-minus-rejected response-feature activation densities.

name: Sparse Activation Steering (SAS)
description: Behavioral steering through frequency-filtered, polarity-exclusive SAE-code contrasts, nonlinear code editing, and reconstruction-residual restoration.

name: Selective SSM hidden attention
description: Input-conditioned causal token-mixing matrices obtained by unrolling selective state-space recurrences, with additive channel and state-coordinate decompositions.

name: Mamba-Attribution
description: Class-specific relevance maps formed from hidden selective-SSM mixing matrices and Mamba block-output gradients, then aggregated across layers.

name: Data-controlled token mixing
description: Architectural analysis distinguishing fixed cross-token mixing, input-dependent tokenwise gates, and input-dependent cross-token transition products.

name: Temporal Feature Analysis
description: An activation decomposition combining attention-derived contextual codes with sparse residual codes, reconstructed through a shared dictionary.

name: Activation nonstationarity
description: Changes in activation distributions, second-moment structure, and temporal similarities with sequence position.

name: Temporal straightening
description: The organization of sequential representations into smoother trajectories, assessed here through embeddings and tortuosity.

name: Second-moment effective dimension
description: Order-two effective rank of normalized activation second moments, estimated through reciprocal mean squared pairwise cosine similarity.

name: Texture vs. shape bias in CNNs
description: Tendency of a classifier to decide by local texture rather than global object shape when the two cues conflict.

name: Cue-conflict stimulus evaluation
description: Behavioural test that pits two cues (e.g. texture vs shape via style transfer) against each other to measure which one drives a classifier's or human's decision.

name: Stylized-ImageNet
description: ImageNet with textures replaced by random painting styles via AdaIN style transfer, removing predictive local texture cues.

name: Post-instruction template-token refusal signal
description: Harmfulness/refusal-relevant information written by attention heads into chat-template token positions after the user instruction (e.g. the [/INST] tokens) in early-to-middle layers.

name: Embedding-space parameter projection
description: Zero-pass interpretation of all Transformer weights (FF keys/values, QK/OV interaction matrices, subheads) by projecting them onto the vocabulary via the embedding matrix and its approximate inverse E^T.

name: Source nonstationarity
description: Latent source distributions (e.g. variances or exponential-family parameters) that change across time segments, exploited as a signal for identifying independent components.

name: Agentic neuron interpretation
description: Using LLM-based agents or automated scientists to investigate and explain individual neurons and circuits at scale, iteratively forming and testing hypotheses rather than relying on a single explain-and-score pass.

name: Conditional computation
description: Activating only parts of a network on a per-example basis to increase capacity without proportional compute.

name: Noisy top-k gating
description: Sparse MoE router that adds learned input-dependent Gaussian noise to gating logits, keeps the top-k and applies softmax.

name: Expert load-balancing losses
description: Auxiliary losses (importance and load coefficient-of-variation penalties) that prevent routers from collapsing onto a few experts.

name: Single-direction reliance
description: How much a network's performance depends on individual units or directions in activation space, measured by cumulative ablation or per-unit noise.

name: Cumulative unit ablation curves
description: Clamping progressively larger random subsets of units or feature maps to a fixed value and tracking accuracy; the area under the curve summarizes robustness.

name: Batch normalization
description: Normalizing activations by minibatch statistics during training.

name: Crowdsourced agent-driven neuron labeling
description: Public participants (livestream chat or GitHub contributors) steer LLM agents to hypothesize, test, and falsify labels for individual neurons, with pre-committed tests, near-miss controls, CI re-scoring and clean-room replication.

name: Bipolar neuron poles
description: Treating the positive and negative activation directions of a gated-MLP neuron as separately interpretable units that can carry unrelated meanings.

name: Quantized LLMs as interpretability model organisms
description: Using heavily quantized (e.g. 1-bit) derivatives of open LLMs as cheap, widely runnable targets for interpretability research.

name: Strategic deception
description: A model attempting to induce false beliefs in users or overseers as an instrumental strategy to pursue a goal, e.g. concealing insider trading or sandbagging evaluations.

name: HarmBench
description: Standardized benchmark of 510 harmful behaviors (standard, contextual, copyright, multimodal) with fixed evaluation pipeline and held-out Llama-2-based ASR classifier.

name: Automated red teaming
description: Automatically generating test cases (optimization, attacker LLMs, templates) to elicit specified harmful behaviors from target models.

name: Robust Refusal Dynamic Defense (R2D2)
description: Adversarial training on a persistent, continually GCG-updated pool of test cases, with away/toward-refusal losses plus SFT.

name: Remove And Retrain (ROAR)
description: Attribution evaluation that removes top-ranked input features from train and test data, retrains from scratch, and measures the resulting accuracy drop.

name: VarGrad
description: Attribution computed as the variance of attribution maps over Gaussian-noised copies of the input.

name: Multimodal neurons
description: Individual units in vision-language models (e.g. CLIP) that respond to the same concept across photographs, drawings, symbols and rendered text, analogous to concept cells in the human brain.

name: Typographic attacks
description: Adversarial attacks on vision models that read text, made by placing rendered or handwritten text on an image to change its classification.

name: Agreement attractors
description: Nouns that intervene between subject and verb with the opposite grammatical number, which mislead linear-order heuristics for agreement.

name: Agreement attraction
description: Errors in which a verb or anaphor agrees with an intervening, structurally irrelevant noun (attractor) rather than its true controller.

name: Syntactic multitask scaffolding
description: Training a language model jointly with a supervised syntactic auxiliary task (e.g., CCG supertagging) to induce better syntactic representations.

name: JailbreakBench / JBB-Behaviors
description: Open benchmark of 100 harmful and 100 topic-matched benign behaviors, with jailbreak artifacts, a standardized judge, defense wrappers and a leaderboard.

name: Jailbreak success judges
description: Automated classifiers (string matching, safeguard models, LLM-as-judge) that decide whether a model response constitutes a successful jailbreak.

name: Test-time jailbreak defenses
description: Inference-time wrappers such as SmoothLLM, perplexity filtering and Erase-and-Check that detect or neutralize jailbreak prompts without retraining.

name: Gradient saturation in attribution
description: Failure of gradient-based importance methods to credit inputs whose effects pass through inactive (ReLU) or saturated (sigmoid/tanh) units with zero or vanishing local gradients.

name: Onion representations
description: Non-linear encoding in which sequence elements are stored as the same token directions at different position-specific magnitudes in a shared subspace, decoded by iteratively peeling off the dominant layer via autoregressive feedback.

name: Nonce (colorless green) sentence evaluation
description: Evaluating syntactic predictions on grammatical but meaningless sentences built by substituting content words with random morphologically matched words, removing lexical-semantic cues.

name: Counterfactual intervention-prediction evaluation
description: Human evaluation in which participants use an explanation to predict which of several input interventions (e.g. occlusions) changes a unit's activation more, as an operational test of causal understanding.

name: Human-centered interpretability evaluation
description: Evaluating explanation methods through controlled human studies of their utility in downstream decision-making tasks.

name: HIVE (Human Interpretability of Visual Explanations)
description: Open-source human-study framework with agreement and distinction tasks for cross-method evaluation of visual explanations.

name: Explanation-induced overtrust
description: Users accepting model predictions as correct when shown explanations, including for incorrect predictions (confirmation bias).

name: Prototype-based interpretable models
description: Interpretable-by-design classifiers (e.g., ProtoPNet, ProtoTree) that reason by matching image regions to learned training-set prototypes.

name: Strict Interchange Intervention Training (SIIT)
description: Extension of IIT that additionally resample-ablates low-level nodes not aligned to any high-level variable and penalizes output changes, so non-circuit components become causally inert on the task distribution.

name: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL)
description: Training a single embedding with task losses summed over nested prefixes of logarithmically spaced sizes so each prefix is an independently usable representation.

name: Coarse-to-fine nested representations
description: Representations whose leading coordinates carry coarse information and later coordinates add finer distinctions.

name: Latent Scaling
description: Closed-form per-latent least-squares scaling of a fine-tuned-model decoder direction to base vs fine-tuned activations, reconstructions and errors. It detects spurious model-specific crosscoder latents.

name: Latent Decoupling in crosscoders
description: A shared concept represented by a model-only latent plus other (e.g. twin) latents in the other model, which is loss-equivalent under L1 crosscoder sparsity.

name: Emergent-misalignment training phase transition
description: An abrupt rotation of learned fine-tuning directions, accompanied by a gradient-norm peak, during which the direction needed for emergent misalignment is acquired; it is revealed behaviourally by scaling the adapter.

name: Persona selection model (PSM)
description: Theory that pre-training yields a distribution over simulable personas and post-training selects and refines an Assistant persona whose traits largely determine AI assistant behavior and generalization.

name: Persona leakage
description: Expression of Assistant persona traits or preferences in LLM generations outside the Assistant turn, e.g. in Human-turn or non-chat continuations.

name: Distractor-feature sanity checks for knowledge probes
description: Evaluating unsupervised knowledge-elicitation methods by inserting controlled non-knowledge binary features (random words, character opinions) into prompts and measuring whether probes track them instead of ground truth.

name: StrongREJECT benchmark
description: Curated 313-prompt forbidden-prompt dataset plus rubric/fine-tuned evaluator scoring non-refusal × specificity and convincingness of jailbroken responses.

name: Jailbreak capability degradation
description: Jailbreak prompt transformations that increase willingness to answer forbidden prompts tend to reduce the model's ability to answer well.

name: TRAIT personality benchmark
description: 8K-item scenario-based multiple-choice LLM personality test for the Big Five and Dark Triad, built from BFI/SD-3 seeds and ATOMIC10x situations.

name: Dark Triad personality traits
description: Machiavellianism, narcissism and psychopathy, measured e.g. via the Short Dark Triad (SD-3).

name: Effects of code in pretraining data
description: How including source code in LM pretraining corpora changes downstream capabilities such as state tracking.

name: Shortcut-controlled state-tracking evaluation
description: Designing entity-state tracking tasks that block lexical, distributional, initial-state-copying and slot-filling heuristics.

name: Semantic priors vs. input–label mappings in ICL
description: The distinction between ICL driven by pretrained knowledge of label/task semantics and ICL driven by learning the exemplar input–label mapping.

name: Semantically-unrelated label ICL (SUL-ICL)
description: ICL evaluation in which natural-language labels are replaced by arbitrary symbols (e.g., Foo/Bar), so success requires learning the input–label mapping from exemplars.

name: Flipped-label ICL
description: ICL evaluation in which exemplar labels are inverted, so that following the exemplars yields below-chance accuracy against ground truth.

name: Emergent abilities with scale
description: Capabilities that appear only in sufficiently large models and are near chance in smaller ones.

name: Instruction tuning
description: Fine-tuning pretrained LMs on collections of tasks phrased as instructions, often with few-shot exemplars.

name: Counterfactual simulation test
description: Human-subject test in which users, given an input, the model's output and an explanation, predict the model's output on a perturbed version of the input; compared against a no-explanation baseline.

name: Anchor rule explanations
description: High-precision, model-agnostic local rule lists learned with PAC-style sampling around an input (Ribeiro et al. 2018).

name: Underspecification
description: A pipeline admits many predictors with equivalent iid held-out risk but different inductive biases, so arbitrary choices determine deployment behavior.

name: Stress-test evaluation
description: Stratified, shifted, and contrastive evaluations that probe whether a predictor satisfies application-specific behavioral contracts not checked by iid evaluation.

name: LLM-as-a-judge
description: Using a strong LLM to evaluate open-ended model responses via pairwise comparison, single-answer grading, or reference-guided grading, as a proxy for human preference.

name: LLM judge biases
description: Systematic errors of LLM evaluators, including position bias, verbosity bias, self-enhancement bias, and being misled by candidate answers.

name: MT-Bench
description: 80 two-turn open-ended questions across 8 categories for evaluating chat assistants, typically scored by GPT-4.

name: Chatbot Arena
description: Crowdsourced platform of anonymous pairwise chatbot battles yielding human preference votes and Elo-style rankings.

name: Optimal ablation (OA)
description: Replacing a component with a single input-independent constant optimized to minimize the ablated model's divergence from the full model on a subtask.

name: Uniform Gradient Sampling (UGS)
description: Circuit discovery by learning per-edge inclusion probabilities using gradients at uniformly sampled partial-ablation coefficients.

name: Optimal Constant Attention (OCA) lens
description: Latent prediction by optimally ablating all later attention layers at the last token position and running the remaining MLPs.

name: Unsupervised steering adapters
description: Rank-r LoRA perturbations of a layer's MLP output weights trained with the unsupervised activation-difference objective, giving steering directions that depend linearly on hidden activations.

name: High-impact features are structurally important
description: Feature-selection principle: directions that induce abnormally large downstream activation change per unit norm are likely used by the model's computation, and can be found without a large dataset.

name: CausalGym
description: Benchmark of 29 templated English minimal-pair linguistic tasks, adapted from SyntaxGym, for scoring interpretability methods by the causal efficacy of interventions on the directions they find.

name: Prompt format sensitivity
description: Variation in LLM task performance under meaning-preserving changes to prompt formatting (separators, spacing, casing, enumeration style).

name: FormatSpread
description: Grammar of plausible equivalent prompt formats plus Thompson-sampling bandit search that estimates the min–max accuracy interval across formats without model weights.

name: Multiple-choice option-order sensitivity
description: Changes in LLM answers and accuracy when the answer options of a multiple-choice question are permuted.

name: Positional bias in LLM option selection
description: A tendency to favour candidates based on their position in the prompt, especially among near-tied options.

name: Permutation majority voting
description: Aggregating predictions over multiple random option orderings to reduce order sensitivity.

name: Believable agents
description: Artificial characters designed to give users the illusion of life, i.e., to be perceived as having coherent personalities, emotions and intentions, rather than to be maximally intelligent or realistic.

name: Anthropomorphic linguistic cues in dialogue systems
description: Voice, content, stylistic and role-based features of system output (e.g. disfluencies, first-person pronouns, pseudo-empathy, phatic expressions, personas, claims of embodied activity) that lead users to personify dialogue systems.

name: Conversational AI safety
description: Risks arising from deployed dialogue systems, including over-reliance, deception, harmful advice and representational harms.

name: Unsupervised steering vectors
description: Fixed-norm residual-stream biases at an early layer optimized to maximize change in later-layer activations relative to the unsteered model.

name: Conflict adaptation
description: Improved performance on a high-conflict trial when it follows another high-conflict trial (congruency sequence / Gratton effect), a signature of cognitive-control recruitment.

name: Sequential Stroop task
description: Paradigm in which a model or participant names the ink color of color words across consecutive congruent/incongruent trials, used to measure interference and sequential conflict effects.

name: SAE/transcoder coactivation supernodes
description: Connected components of cross-layer sparse-feature networks built from token-level coactivation, used as task-relevant feature groups for ablation.

name: CKA manipulability and subset-translation sensitivity
description: Linear (and RBF) CKA can be driven to arbitrary values via function-preserving transformations such as translating a subset of representations or outliers, or by directly optimizing a CKA map while distilling outputs.

name: FeatureEdit
description: Knowledge-erasure method that zeroes MLP down-projection weight positions where the decoder directions of selected SAE features have large magnitude.

name: Feature Steering with Reinforcement Learning (FSRL)
description: A lightweight input-dependent adapter, trained on a preference objective, outputs sparse signed modulations of SAE features at one layer of a frozen LLM; the result is decoded and added to the residual stream.

name: Style hacking
description: A form of reward hacking in which preference optimization reduces loss mainly by manipulating presentation and formatting features rather than improving semantic content.

name: Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO)
description: Reference-free preference optimization using a length-normalized Bradley-Terry loss with a target reward margin.

name: Metalinguistic prompting
description: Evaluating linguistic knowledge by asking a model, in natural language, for judgments about linguistic expressions (e.g. grammaticality, next-word likelihood) rather than reading out string probabilities.

name: Competence–performance distinction in LLMs
description: The proposal that the information in an LLM's string probability distribution (competence) can diverge from its behavior when prompted (performance).

name: Functional grounding of representation similarity measures
description: Evaluating dissimilarity measures by rank correlation of their distances with differences in functional behavior (probing accuracy, OOD accuracy), framed as sensitivity/specificity.

name: Judge leniency bias
description: Tendency of LLM judges to label responses as correct when their evaluation does not follow the given criteria.

name: Chance-corrected agreement metrics (Scott's π, Cohen's κ)
description: Inter-rater agreement statistics that subtract expected chance agreement, used to compare judges with humans.

name: TriviaQA
description: Trivia question-answering dataset with short reference answers.

name: Explanation information overload
description: Exposing more model detail (internals, many features) can divert attention from unusual input properties and impair human judgment.

name: Reliance on algorithmic advice
description: How closely people follow model predictions, measured e.g. by deviation or weight of advice; includes algorithm aversion and appreciation.

name: Measurement invariance
description: Requirement that a test's psychometric function (factor loadings, intercepts, residuals) relating latent traits to item responses is identical across populations; tested with multi-group CFA.

name: Acquiescence (agree) bias
description: Tendency to agree with questionnaire items regardless of content, detectable via inconsistent answers to true- and false-keyed items.

name: Confirmatory factor analysis
description: Fitting a hypothesized sparse factor model to item responses and assessing fit (CFI, TLI, RMSEA), used to check structural validity and as a prerequisite for interpreting reliability coefficients.

name: LLM survey response elicitation
description: Obtaining LLM answer distributions to survey questions from renormalized answer-label token probabilities and comparing them with human population statistics.

name: Survey-derived population alignment metrics
description: Scores of how similar a model's survey answer distributions are to those of demographic or national subgroups (e.g. OpinionQA, GlobalOpinionQA).

name: Choice-order randomization adjustment
description: Averaging model answer distributions over permutations of answer-to-label assignments to remove ordering and labeling biases.

name: Silicon sampling / synthetic survey respondents
description: Using LLMs to generate synthetic human survey respondents.

name: RISE (Randomized Input Sampling for Explanation)
description: Black-box saliency method that estimates pixel importance as the score-weighted average of random smooth masks applied to the input, normalized by the mask expectation.

name: Deletion and insertion attribution metrics
description: Attribution evaluation by the area under the class-probability curve as attribution-ranked pixels are progressively removed (deletion) or restored onto a blurred canvas (insertion).

name: Garçon
description: Anthropic's internal server/client infrastructure for remotely hosting large (multi-GPU, multi-node) models. It exposes named probe points where user-supplied functions can read, modify, aggregate, or take gradients through internal activations.

name: Remote activation hooks / probe points
description: Named intervention sites in a hosted model where serialized user code executes server-side during forward or backward passes. The code can save, reduce, or replace tensors.

name: Virtual attention heads
description: Effective attention operations arising from composition of heads in different layers, whose OV map is the product of the constituent heads' OV matrices and whose attention pattern is the product of their patterns.

name: High-level action features
description: Hypothesized output-side features in language models that trigger coordinated behaviors spanning multiple tokens, analogous to motor neurons.

name: Emergent discretization of feature manifolds
description: Tendency of networks to represent a continuous feature manifold (e.g., a circle of orientations) with a family of discrete units, each covering a region of the manifold, rather than with a continuous coordinate code.

name: Spatiotemporal representations in LLMs
description: Internal representations encoding real-world geographic location and temporal position of entities and events.

name: Space and time neurons
description: Individual MLP neurons whose weights align with linear probe directions for spatial or temporal coordinates and whose activations track those coordinates.

name: MILANNOTATIONS
description: Dataset of about 60k human natural-language descriptions of masked top-activating exemplar sets for about 20k neurons from 7 vision models.

name: Switch sparse autoencoders
description: SAE architecture in which a trainable softmax router sends each activation to a single small TopK expert SAE, scaling the expert output by the router probability; trained with reconstruction MSE plus a load-balancing auxiliary loss.

name: Attribution dictionary learning
description: Dictionary learning whose objective also penalises the L1 norm of feature attributions (activation × loss gradient) and unexplained attribution in the reconstruction error, so that features are sparse both as representations and as actions on the output.

name: Magnitude-coded features
description: Distinct mutually exclusive features encoded by different activation magnitudes of a single unit, decoded via softmax over affine readouts.

name: Acceptability classification
description: Training or evaluating models to make Boolean grammatical-acceptability judgments on individual sentences, as a behavioral test of grammatical competence.

name: Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (CoLA)
description: 10,657 English sentences from linguistics literature with expert acceptability labels, split into in-domain and out-of-domain sources.

name: Relational composition
description: Mechanisms by which networks combine feature vectors into representations of ordered or structured relationships beyond unordered feature sets.

name: Additive matrix binding
description: Binding ordered vectors as r = A x + B y with fixed distinct matrices, equivalent to writing into superposed slots.

name: Vector symbolic architectures (VSA)
description: Family of vector binding schemes, such as tensor-product/outer-product projections and binary XOR-permutation codes, for representing compositional structure.

name: REMEDI (representation mediation)
description: Learned affine map from an LM's encoding of a textual attribute to an additive edit of a single entity-token hidden state. It is trained causally with target, prior-suppression and KL losses. The learned directions can also be used as probes.

name: Linear layer-shortcut mappings (mat)
description: Least-squares linear maps fitted from hidden states at one transformer layer to those at a later layer, used to bypass intermediate computation for interpretation or early exit.

name: Neural network dark matter (unresolved rare features)
description: The hypothesized large population of extremely rare and sparse features, including memorization features, that current dictionary learning cannot resolve but which may make up most features.

name: Feature sensitivity evaluation via LLM dataset filtering
description: Estimating P(feature fires | concept present) by using an LLM to rate concept relevance across a broad corpus and then measuring feature firing on high-relevance samples.
